Had PEA cardiac arrest x4 secondary to bilateral massive PE with right heart strain.  Received systemic thrombolysis 9/17.  Initially in shock, likely obstcutive, and requiring pressors, though this did improve after a few days and patient came off pressors.  Also initially with metabolic/lactic acidosis, likely secondary to PEA arrest hypoperfusion.  Labs monitored with resolution.  Post arrest echo with mildly reduced EF and dilated RV.  No DVT on lower extremity Dopplers.  PE possibly provoked secondary to recent COVID-19 vaccination, though hematology felt to be unprovoked.    There was initially some concern for vaccine induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia secondary to patient's recent receipt of the COVID vaccine as well as thrombocytopenia.  Pf4 antibodies and serotonin release assay sent per hematology recommendation, and patient was started on argatroban for anticoagulation.  Pf4 and SRA negative with improved platelet count, so patient was transitioned to heparin infusion and remained on this throughout the course of his hospitalization.  Patient also initially with DIC, received cryoprecipitate, and labs were monitored with resolution.  He was not cooled given concerns for increased risk of bleeding secondary to DIC, thrombocytopenia, receipt of tPA.   The patient continued to require intubation and mechanical ventilation.  Initially secondary to massive PE/PEA arrest.  Continued predominantly secondary poor mental status secondary to anoxic brain injury and extremely high doses of sedating medication to control seizures.  The patient developed severely refractory seizures secondary to anoxic brain injury.  Initial EEG demonstrated status epilepticus.  He eventually required multiple antiepileptic medications as well as very deep sedation to achieve suppression. Critical Care were consulted and followed patient's course, providing recommendation.  Patient was also kept continuous EEG.  Patient was taken for MRI on 09/20 after he was sufficiently stabilized, notable for anoxic brain injury.  CT head obtained 9/27 stable, no acute abnormalities.  Ammonia level mildly elevated, not enough to explain cognitive deficit.  Per neuro recommendation, LP was not felt to be necessary given the predominantly etiology of anoxic brain injury.  Patient also developed primary lung findings of hemopneumothorax, bilateral lower lobe consolidations and pleural effusions.  Bronchoscopy performed 9/22 with removal of large amount of thick mucus, cultures negative.  Bronchoscopy again performed 9/26 with thin secretions, cultures negative.  Patient covered with Zosyn.  Chest tube placed 9/24 for hemothorax, with decrease in the amount of hemothorax confirmed on imaging.  Chest tube remained in place throughout remainder of admission. The patient was additionally found to have bilateral renal infarctions on CT as well as AKI.  Initial AKI most likely secondary to ATN in the setting of cardiac arrest.  He did not require dialysis.  Creatinine plateaued, then improved, though eventually did again worsen, unclear etiology.  Continued to make urine, though was very challenging to fully diurese, particularly given large intake from IV drips as well as hypernatremia.  Patient eventually did again develope a metabolic acidosis, likely secondary to worsened renal function.  Fluid overload caused a large amount of anasarca, particularly abdominal distension/abdominal wall edema.  Abdominal distension was initially thought to be secondary to obstruction, though imaging demonstrated no signs of obstruction and patient had bowel movements.  Patient additionally with a normocytic anemia, predominantly secondary to hemothorax.  Down trended slowly during admission.  Did require transfusion with one unit with appropriate response.  Further issues addressed during patient's hospitalization include hemoperitoneum and lower abdominal mesentery hemorrhage demonstrated on CT 9/17, improved on repeat imaging.  Chest wall fractures additionally noted on CT 9/17, though these did not require management.  The patient also had shock liver with transaminitis, though LFTs trended downward appropriately. Family was kept appraised of patient's condition and poor prognosis, particularly given severe brain injury.  Caregiving assisted, and patient's family made the decision to refrain from escalating care on 9/30.  Planned to withdraw care likely the following day once further family had had time to come and see the patient.  Patient had a worsening acidosis as well as FiO2 requirement overnight 9/30 to 10/1.  Bicarb drip was held as decision had been made for no escalation of care.  Patient expired on 10/1 at 0700.

I went on a liquid only diet to help keep hydrated and stop the diarrhea. On day 5, I woke up with very red and hot hands and feet. They were painful to the touch. On day 7, I had my first 'real' meal and notice the redness and pain were replaced with a measles like rash on my hands. Which caused constipation. On day 6 and the 2 days following, I didn't have a fever, my hands and feet had returned to normal, but itched, and I didn't have many symptoms, but felt very sluggish and fatigued. Female 15-year old client received her first Pfizer shot (Lot# EW0185) at 15:02.  She was accompanied by her mother and 12-year-old sister, who was also vaccinated at the same station with her. RN1 stated that from the opposite end of the hallway she saw client?s knees buckle.  RN1 walked toward client to ask if she was OK.  Client straightened herself out, slumped onto her mother?s shoulder, and rolled onto her mother, who guided client to the floor.  At 15:09 Lead RN heard client fall to the floor, went out to the client, and radioed for EMT assistance. Client was conscious and turned her face up.  Client?s mother stated client passed out for 2-3 seconds and that her head did not hit the floor.  Client?s mother stated that she cushioned her fall.  Client was breathing adequately, appeared pale in face and lips, and stated she was OK.  Lead RN and RN1 kept client lying on the floor and elevated her legs on a chair.  EMT1 & EMT2 arrived at 15:10 and checked client?s pulse (HR:  74).  Client denied head, neck, and back pain.  Client was alert & oriented times 3 (person, place, & event).  Client stated she was OK to stand up and sit in a wheelchair.  Wheeled client to extra vacant breakroom where client vitals were taken by EMT2 at 15:17 (BP:  124/60, HR:  96).  EMT1?s assessment found the client exhibited good circulation, sensation, and motor function in all 4 extremities.  Client denied chest pain, shortness of breath, and nausea & vomiting.  Client was leaning forward in the wheelchair resting her elbows on her lap.  She stated she does not remember becoming nonresponsive and that she felt dizzy when lying her head back.  Client stated she has a history of anxiety and panic attacks and is currently taking Prozac.  Client stated she felt hot.  Client?s mother stated client ate a full lunch at 12:35. At 15:20 Lead RN provided client with a bottle of water.  Lead RN & EMT also observed client?s color returning to her face at that time.  Client sat upright and stated that she felt better and was alert & oriented times 4.  Client and mother declined going to the hospital and calling 911 for evaluation.  At 15:23 client was wheeled to the observation room with her mother and sister where she remained seated in the wheelchair for 30 minutes for additional observation by EMT1.  At 1600 EMT1 took client vitals while she was seated (BP:  116/82, HR:  68, RR:  16).  EMT1 took client vitals again while having client stand (BP:  120/86, HR:  72, RR:  16).  Client and mother stated they were OK to go home.  Client and mother were instructed by Lead RN to follow up with HCP if client experienced any additional symptoms after going home and to call 911 if client experienced SOB or any difficulties breathing.  Lead RN and EMT observed client leave the facility walking with a steady gait with her mother and sister.

I contacted my Dr. immediately the morning of Wednesday, January 6th and after assessing me she felt it was a skin infection. She prescribed Doxycycline antibiotic and Zyrtec by day, Benadryl by night.  I began the antibiotic treatment with first dose on 1/6/21 at 1:30 p.m., dose 2 9:00 p.m. and dose 3 on Thursday, January 7th 2020 around 8:00 a.m.  I have responded well to the treatment and already my arm is much improved.  My Dr. felt it could have been the technique of the administration of the vaccine that caused infection.  However, I wanted to report in case anyone else with this batch also experienced similar response.

She got her vaccine, had no reactions.   She woke up on 5/12/21 and had extreme headache, blood pressure was high, nausea and vomiting, extreme pain behind her eyes, blurry vision.  Later in the afternoon she had diarrhea.  She called her PCP that evening and he prescribed Ondansetron (Zofran).  On Thursday she continued to have the blurred and double vision with some nausea and dizziness and headaches which have been on-going, especially on the left side of her head.    She went to the ER on Friday evening 5/14/21 where her BP at it's highest point was 195/126 and a pulse of 99.   They started doing some actions to determine if she was having a stroke.  They did a CT scan and gave her medications to get her BP down, started an IV.  She was then admitted to HCF that evening.   They kept her overnight and did an MRI on 5/15/21, had to start wearing an eye patch on her left eye due to dizziness and was not able to walk without covering the one eye and needed assistance to walk across the room.   Everything was clear on the MRI and CAT scan.  She saw two resident internist and then she saw a neurologist while being in the hospital.  The neurologist diagnosed her with left third nerve palsy as a result from the vaccine and the high BP.  They released her that evening with instructions to see an Ophthalmologist the following week, which she did on 5/17/21 and saw Dr.  He concurred with the neurologist diagnosis and felt that there was really nothing that they needed to do and for it to run it's course and let it heal which will take anywhere from 2 weeks to 4 months.  She was informed to continue to wear the eye patch until the dizziness and double vision improve.  There is pain still behind the left eye, and still has high BP and have prescribed medications for that.   Her PCP started her on Amlodipine/HCTZ 10/12.5 mg.     She then ended up in the ER again last night on 5/19/21.  They put her on fluids as she started vomiting again and could not keep any of the medications down that she was prescribed.  So they gave her fluids and started a steroid in the IV fluids to help with the pain and inflammation behind her eye, as well as headache medications as well.  She was then sent home last night and now the pain in her eye is about a 5 since receiving the steroids.  She was also started on Prednisone 20 mg to start today as when she was in the ER they told her to start that.   She has not had any nausea or vomiting today, and seems to be OK, but is still taking the Zofran for this.  She was able to eat a little bit today and hold it down, but has not had much in the way of an appetite since receiving the vaccine.

I started taking my husband's hydrocodone to sleep and continue daily function. Each day, my arm improved, however, I was no longer able to lift or move it with real intent. (It was like it was paralyzed)The weirdest things that my hand (fist) was never affected. I could use it as long as I did not have to move my arm or bend my elbow. By then I was no longer taking pain pills but I did not have full range of motion. Now, April 27th, I can lift my arm up with no pain but my strength is still weak. Patient states that, on evening after receiving booster dose of Moderna vaccine, she developed bloody diarrhea. These symptoms persisted for weeks. Pt. presented to emergency department on 11/22/2021 with complaints of GI discomfort, blood in stool, straining, and constipation. She was diagnosed with acute colitis and discharged from the ED with a prescription for antibiotics.  Pt presented to her outpatient provider on 11/30 with the same chief complaint. Diagnosis of colitis remained unchanged, and patient was prescribed a new 10-day course of antibiotics.  On 12/7, patient presented to the emergency department again with worsening symptoms of colitis, diarrhea, blood in stool, and GI discomfort. She was subsequently admitted for the next 24 days for major surgery with significant co-morbid complications, including:  Hypercoagulable state (new) Ischemic colitis Cerebrovascular infarction, embolic (new) New cardiomyopathy, +troponin/NSTEMI- Acute blood loss anemia PUD/gastritis/duodenitis Hypervolemia Marked hypoalbuminemia Ascites Dysphagia Severe malnutrition AKI, resolved Deconditioning  On 12/14, the patient underwent a near total colectomy with ileostomy due to new-onset ischemic colitis. Pathological analysis was conducted by providers from both Medical Center and the Health System. This reporting is below:                                                                      Diagnosis:  Terminal ileum, cecum with appendix, and colon, subtotal colectomy: Segmental active colitis with multifocal ulceration, focal pseudomembrane formation, and areas of ischemic-type mucosal injury. Associated prominent and extensive microvascular thrombosis.  See comment. Comment: Sections demonstrate contiguous involvement of the colon by a process of active colitis involving both lamina propria and crypts, areas of exudative luminal inflammation, and submucosal abscesses. While some changes of chronicity are evident, this is less than would typically be present in an inflammatory bowel disease.  The most striking feature of the process is the presence of extensive microvascular thrombosis involving both larger vessels in the submucosa and extending into small vessels in the mucosa.  In a few sections, entire vascular trees appear to be involved.  These areas are associated with ischemic-type mucosal injury.  Sections of lymph nodes also demonstrate focal microvascular thrombosis.  Because this is a very unusual colitis, the case is discussed with the attending hospitalist caring for the patient who indicates that there is an unusual clinical setting as well. Because of this, the case will be forwarded to the University for consultative opinion.  When available, this will be reported in an addendum.  Procedures/Addenda: Addendum  Date Ordered:12/22/2021 Status:Signed Out   Date Complete:12/22/2021   Date Reported:12/23/2021 15:56  Addendum Diagnosis Following examination of the glass slides at Medical Center, this case was forwarded in consultation to Laboratories, whose report reads:  "DIAGNOSIS: Colon, subtotal colectomy (12/14/2021):  Severely active chronic colitis resembling ulcerative colitis with extensive venous thrombi affecting distal colon.  Terminal ileum and proximal colon spared.  Sixteen benign lymph nodes with scattered thrombi.  See comment.  The colonic mucosa demonstrates changes resembling ulcerative colitis.  This is characterized by diffuse involvement of mainly the distal aspect of the colon by inflammation, villous elongation with crypt architectural distortion, lamina propria lymphoplasmacytosis, and crypt abscesses.  There are some areas of marked hemorrhage; otherwise usual features of ischemia, such as withered crypts, lamina propria hemorrhage, followed by fibrosis, are not present.  Moreover, ischemia typically does not have so much active inflammation.  What is unusual is the striking presence of transmural organizing venous thrombi. Ulcerative colitis does have an association with hypercoagulability and I have seen ulcerative colitis cases with thrombi, but I cannot exclude the possibility of thrombi associated with the vaccine, which also appears to have isolated reports of hypercoagulability as a complication.  Finally, we have encountered gastrointestinal thrombi as a systemic complication of COVID-19 itself. As such, the possibilities in this case include hypercoagulability related to the chronic colitis, the vaccine, or, if the patient actually had COVID-19 during this time, SARS-CoV-2.  I shared this unusual case with Dr. as well as with my other GI pathology colleagues at our daily GI pathology consensus conference.  They agree that this case has features identical to ulcerative colitis and the etiology for the findings, including the thrombi, is unclear but still may be related to the vaccine. symptom_text: Yesterday, approximately two weeks after my vaccination, I had a dozen grilled shrimp for dinner and had a pretty severe allergic reaction.  I had itching, hives, swelling around one eye and under my chin.  I have never had an allergic reaction to any food before.  I took a benadryl immediately at onset of symptoms and a second one before bed.  It helped control the itching but now even 24 hours later the swelling is just starting to go down.   Obviously I have no idea if this was due to the vaccine or not but it seems very coincidental that this would happen for the first time in my life within two weeks of getting the shot,  I still plan to get the second shot but will avoid shellfish for some time.

symptom_text: On 9/28/2022, I was exposed to COVID-19. On 10/1/2022, I went to a party at noon. While I was there, I noticed my nose was running a little, and I had a slight tickle in the back of the throat. After about an hour, I left and went home. I took a nap and ended up sleeping until the morning of 10/2/2022. When I woke up, I had a painful, burning sensation in the back of the throat, plus phlegm. This continued for about five days and then began to subside. I was not able to function for another week. On 10/2/2022, I took a home antigen test and got a positive result. I had a telehealth visit with a local urgent care clinic on 10/3/2022, and I was prescribed Paxlovid, which I began taking 10/6/2022. I had no perceived improvement after beginning the medicine, but my symptoms also did not worsen. I took OTC Mucinex and Ricola lozenges to help treat the symptoms, but they weren't very effective. After about a week, I began to feel a little better. I felt much better after two weeks, but it took a month before I felt like I was back to normal. On 11/30/2022, I was again exposed to COVID-19. On 12/3/2022, I began to develop a sore throat, but it was less intense than it had been in October. I thought I had strep throat. I had sore throat and runny nose that continued for several days, but I powered through them and continued with my normal activities. Since I had recently had COVID-19, I didn't think I could possibly get it again so soon. On 12/9/2022, I went to a local urgent care clinic to undergo a strep test. A throat swab was performed, and I was given a brief physical exam before I was sent home. I learned within minutes after being tested that I was negative for streptococcus, but on 12/10/2022, I found out that I had tested positive for COVID-19 and RSV. I was offered Paxlovid, but I decided not to take it, because my symptoms this time around were less severe than they had been the first time around. I just treated my symptoms with OTC Mucinex and Ricola lozenges, but they didn't seem to help much. Because the symptoms were less severe this time, I was able to function well enough to work from home. I just took lots of naps and slept a lot. The symptoms lasted for about two weeks. It took a full month before I returned to my pre-COVID-19 functioning level.

symptom_text: After the first vaccination, I had fever, chills, fatigue, etc. About 23 hours after the 2nd vaccination, I had severe vertigo. I woke up that morning feeling fine and was happy to have no adverse effects. At about 10AM, I started feeling a little dizzy. I had had vertigo about 5 years prior so got on the floor to do a maneuver hoping that would help. When I stood up, the room turned black, and my head started spinning fast. I made it to the couch but fell into it facing the back. About 30 minutes later, I started vomiting all over the couch and myself but because of the spinning, I could not move. I called 911. The EMTs took my vitals which were fine and gave me an anti-nausea pill. I dozed off after they left but was still spinning. My son came home at approximately 3PM and helped me from the couch to the bathroom then to the bed. A few hours after that, I could walk to the bathroom on my own but only by staring at the floor. The next day, I could walk into the kitchen staring at the floor. That night I woke up around 2AM spinning, but it went away in an hour or so.  Since then I have not had the severe spinning, but I cannot move my head quickly and have a general feeling of heaviness in my head. I did not drive for several months, and started to get anxiety. I am driving now, but I cannot drive long distances.

symptom_text: I went to the hospital due to shortness of breath and extreme pressure and pain in my chest, specifically surrounding my heart, diaphram, and radiating up to my collar bones and shoulders. I was taken for a CAT scan of my upper abdomen and they found that I had a large (650ml) pericardial effusion causing cardiac tampenade. I underwent a procedure that inserted a needle into my pericardium, sucked out the fluid, and inserted a drain tube for 48 hours to drain excess fluid. Upon additional testing, it was determined that I had none of the usual causes for a pericardial effusion (no heart attack or trauma, no infection either viral or bacterial, no cancer, no autoimmune conditions.) My inflammation markers were extremely elevated and my lymph nodes in CAT scan were swollen. As a result, I now have constrictive pericarditis, scar like tissue surrounding my heart constricting its function.

On Sunday, Sept. 11 I woke at my son's home at 6 a.m. unable to open my eyes, could not sit or stand because of violent vertigo and intense nausea. 911 responders took me to local Hospital where I was was admitted as a possible stroke patient. CT determined no cranial bleeding. Severe vertigo continued. I was treated with anti-nausea medications and admitted to the hospital. Dr. Private, was my attending physician, though she is not my primary care doctor as I was visiting my son. I was discharged on Wednesday, Sept. 14, with the diagnosis of no stroke, but no reason for the vertigo. I was referred to vestibular therapist who recommended seeing ENT doctor. On Sept. 21 Dr. diagnosed vestibular neuritis. I am now in PT and am recovering gradually. I also remember having a bad ear ache when I got up to use the bathroom which might have thrown off my balance  I was able to crawl back into my bedroom to get my cellphone. I contacted my parents who live next door. Shortly after they called 911 and paramedics came. They checked my blood pressure and did an EKG. The paramedics didn't feel that it was necessary to drive me to the ER, so I rested in bed for a few hours.  I went to a walk-in clinic where they ran some blood tests and referred me for a CT scan. I took a Covid test prior to going in, it was negative. I then went to Urgent Care to find some answers and get help. The doctors and nurses were great and saw me right away. All of my vitals were normal - good but still puzzling. Then the doctor assessed me. I had no cough or sickness, no injury, I hadn't been exercising vigorously, no indigestion. I am too young for a heart attack. The doctor ruled out is was Costochondritis. The cartilage is irritated and inflamed between the ribs causing painful breathing and pressure. I was given a 5 day prescription of Prednisone, 20 mg twice a day. If it doesn't subside, then we will do x-rays to see if there is a blood clot. I asked the doctor if it could be a side effect of the booster shot since I just had it 12 days prior, they said they didn't think it was that. I don't believe that. Very strange this is happening. The only thing different is I had the shot.

Throughout the first couple of days after taking the vaccine, I experienced tiredness and what I thought was normal arm pain. The first concerning symptoms I had almost a week after the first shot and were shortness of breath and feeling like the top half of my body was swollen. I was worried this was an allergic reaction, since I do have experience with allergic reactions from having a food allergy. Vaccine site became red and largely swollen later that same day so I made an appointment with the walk-in clinic that evening, since it was a weekend. The symptoms I presented, swollen bi-lateral lymph nodes in my chest and under my arm, reminded the PA of cancer or even cat scratch fever so lab work was taken. The staff did find research about similar reactions to Moderna in women that mimicked signs of breast cancer. This reaction seemed to align with how I was presenting. I was prescribed steroids for the following week to help with the swelling. This help a lot and I got the call a week later that my lab work had come back normal.  I took the 2nd vaccine a month later and did not have any concerning side affects and little to no arm pain.  What's weird now, is on September 24th, I developed full body hives throughout the day and my joints began to swell. (the fingers on my hand were twice the size). My entire body wouldn't stop itching. So I took a trip that evening to urgent care again. This time, another location because the was the first appointment available. I had started taking Wellbutrin for anxiety/adhd symptoms earlier that month so that's really the only thing that's changed. I was prescribed another set of steroids and antibiotics in case my symptoms were from lyme disease. I have a follow-up with a rheumatologist because of bloodwork results. I have no idea if this is even relevant to the Moderna COVID vaccine. But I've never had anything like these two occurrences happen before. Totally would take the vaccine over again, I just have no idea what's going on. I figure it helps to document anything weird after.

I had a sweatshirt on over a tee shirt and a heating pad on between the two with two comforters on. At 3 a.m. I had to take ibuprofen (800 mg) because my body hurt too bad to even touch my skin.  My eyelids hurt.  My toes hurt. My ears hurt.  My fever was up to 103.  I fell asleep finally and woke up at 730 a.m. feeling much improved besides some mild chills.  I made the wrong decision to go to work.  I arrived at work at 830 and by 10 a.m. I started to get chilled again, achy and feeling like I was going downhill again.  I decided to go home. Woke up again at 7 p.m. tried to eat something but had no interest and just wanted to sleep.  Throughout the night I would get the sweats that would drench through my t shirt.  The following day, 2 days post 2nd dose I slept all day.  Not as chilled but very tired.  Noticed injection site was now red and swollen, again documented in pictures.  Slept all day.  Today injection site has gotten slightly larger based on markers I marked on my skin, but not as red.  Not too energetic but much improved.

I don't remember if I was at pharmacy at 4pm or 5pm exact.  However, getting the shot, was easy.  I was so shocked how easy it was.  But the aftermath, became a different story.  I had a few small items to purchase at the store.  So, I got up and started walking from the pharmacy over to produce at a fast pace (for me).  Within about 2 minutes, my heart was pounding fast. It scared me. I paused at flowers, took deep breathes, and started moving much slower.  I felt a large, strong adrenaline rush in my body, but heart racing had slowed down.  Since my heart slowed down, I thought, "Ok, I'll get my stuff."  I did.  However, each time I started moving a little faster, my heart would speed up, and that rush feeling would com. ...and that rush feeling would come back.  That concerned me.  Well, I methodically finished purchasing my few items walking slowly.  I checked out and went back over to the pharmacy.  The lady who gave me the injection saw me out of the corner of her eye.  She was busy at one of the customer counters, so I walked over and sat down in the pharmacy chairs nearby.  (I knew if something happened, she would see and help me).  I sat for about 5 - 10 minutes.  She stayed busy.  I decided to drive slowly home.  I got up, spoke with the lady (she said she was coming to check on me as soon as she finished with what she had in her hand). I told her I just wanted to let her know I was going home.  She said ok.  I left.    I went home, arm looked fine.   As long as I moved slowly, deliberately, I was ok.  I went to bed early.  By the next day, a red quarter sized circle appeared on my upper left arm.  I expected that.  Arm was a little sore (expected that).  I went to work the next day.  I tired very quickly, but I was able to do desk work.  My co-workers thought I should have stayed home.  But, I was not willing to get a demerit (point) for being absent for this.  At that time I understood each person was a case by case basis.  I wasn't willing to chance my case.    Here is what I did NOT expect:  the red circle on my upper left growing (bigger than an old silver dollar coin a few times) on my left upper arm that would come and go.  My left arm being warm to the touch.  Also, within a day or so after the shot, I felt a gel "pill" like circle IN my arm about an inch above my elbow.  So, thinking the medicine needed help to move around, I started gently rubbing (massaging) my arm up and down.  While the "gel" like substance disappeared, I started experiencing  black and blue "bruising" in my left arm along with the redness.  I would literally have red, black, and blue "come and go" spots on my arm.  (I did NOT rub for long).  This ended up causing a regression in my left arm among my tendons/ligaments that I thought was healed.  (About a year or two ago, I had some tendon/ligament issues in that arm)  I am not a happy camper.  This went on for a few weeks.  My co-workers told me I needed to get it checked out.  (But I was still alive and able to function, so I guess that is what Moderna and the government would consider:  success??!!)  I (a person who believes in taking vaccines) was angry, frustrated, scared, and wished I had taken the JnJ  or Pfizer vs Moderna.  Then I decided NOT to take the second shot.  This was ridiculous.    I did go to my doctor, but for other issues.  I did mention about getting my shot and what had happened.  He glanced at my arm and said it appeared to be healing.  I told him I may not be getting the second dose.  I asked if we could see about how much antigen/antibiotic I had in my blood in a few weeks.  We wanted to give this a little longer.  Since then, my job is pressuring people to get the vaccine.  I am very, very frustrated.  I do have a Dr's appointment to see how I should proceed.  A few times during these couple of months, when I would go back to do some general shopping, I would stop off at the Pharmacy to ask questions.  I spoke with 3 different people in the pharmacy, explaining my experiences.  1 person mentioned that I should to the Vaers Safe Check-in and sign up (I did), 1 person mentioned they could never get through to Moderna to ask their questions (I'm thinking, but you are a pharmacy calling?!!!).  Another person mentioned, they heard of another customer having the same effects I did.  I left knowing I wasn't the only one.  All would say, to seek medical attention if needed.  Many times I was told, "That may be how YOUR body is reacting."  I'm thinking, but there were TEST trials before the general public started taking it .... and some of my symptoms were NOT mentioned.    As of August 19, 2021, I still have the shot injection mark on my upper left arm.  I do not understand how this is still here.  I get blood draws frequently, and my skin is penetrated to get the Remicaid in, yet those heal up fast (within 24 hours).  The flu shot heals up fast (within 24 hours).  This Moderna shot does NOT.

After I got my first Moderna booster, I had intermittent pre-existing pain that worsened. The pain extended from the back of my thigh toward my knee. The pain was in both legs, but it was worse in the left leg. It felt sort of like sitting on a tennis ball on the left side., and it sometimes caused me trouble walking. My doctor took X-rays, but he found no anomalies, so he guessed it was bursitis. He recommended physical therapy, which I received for about eight weeks. After the therapy sessions ended, I still did the exercises that I had learned. The discomfort was no better or worse than before, but the exercises helped decrease the intensity of the pain. Between May and September 2022, I was fine. I still had some intermittent discomfort, but it didn't interfere with my ability to go about my normal activities. On 9/18/2022, I received my second Moderna booster (AS7143C). The pain returned about three weeks afterwards. The pain was in the same part of the legs that it had been prior to my getting physical therapy, and I also had trouble walking again. I went to an orthopedic surgeon, because I felt like something was wrong. I underwent X-rays, and no structural anomalies were present. The surgeon then told me that it was likely ischial bursitis that had been activated. He then recommended that I get physical therapy, which I didn't start until 4/4/2023. In the meantime, I did the exercises that I had learned in my previous physical therapy sessions. They helped lessen the intensity of the pain, but the skin around my left thigh started to feel tight. I continue to experience the feeling of tightness at the time of this writing. After my first appointment of the day, I had to drop the rest of my plans to rest, and I slept about 16 hours. This also happened after the second dose, but I was unsure if it was related to the vaccine, as I had made several errors with my daily medications that week and had gotten little sleep. This was not the case after third dose, yet the symptoms were worse. After 16 hours of sleep, the symptoms largely subsided, and if boosters were to be offered annually going forward, I would continue to take them despite these symptoms, but the effect on my HR was arguably substantive, so I figured I should report. *I also had soreness at the injection site, which was mild and expected. First of all, GRATEFUL to be getting the vaccine! Surprised how intense and how long lasting side effects have been. Terrible fever, headache, weakness, hives. Fatigue and fever hit first. On first shot (3/26) I'd felt tingles in my mouth (like dental novocaine wearing off) though I have no facial fillers, but do have 2 dental implants. 2nd shot was Friday 4/23/21 11 am, by 1 pm I felt something coming on, but then fatigue took over. Dozed, but by evening, terrible fever hit - lucid dream/nightmares of pain all night, it hurt to move or be touched, but I knew it was the vaccine and would pass. Eventually the fever lessened on Saturday, and I slept better, but the headache worsened -- a migraine settled in and seemed concentrated behind my eyes, at the sides of my face and base of my skull. Hives  came and went. My throat would get sore and then be fine. The headache pain was incapacitating through Sunday night -- I dozed when I could and was feverish but better than I had been. I sipped chicken broth and juice and put a warm wash cloth on my face to ease the pain. Finally I woke in the early hours of Monday and the headache was better, but then when I got up in the morning my eyes were swollen as if I were having intense allergies - big pockets of fluid behind the sockets and my whole face was swollen as it turned out. The fever came and went, the headache returned in the afternoon with eyes very red. I worked from home and did a little exercise (I normally exercise at least an hour elliptical each day, but didn't since Friday as I was too sick); I again went to sleep early and woke Tuesday 4/28 , feeling better still, but I'm sill foggy as if I just recovered from a long flu. I have more energy but waves of fever and fatigue still wash over me. This continued all week, with the headache preventing me from most activity until Saturday May 1st, a full week later, was the first day I felt okay again.

On 11/14/21, I began to feel itchy all over my body, but particularly on my back, chest, feet, and hands. To determine the cause of this, I switched to a sensitive skin laundry detergent and systematically eliminated my soaps in the shower. I also tried moisturizing lotion and anti-itch cream. However, I was unable to find the cause or any relief. Around 2 weeks later, I began to experience hives in the same spots I was having the itching. I am unsure of the exact date, however the first time I took a photo of the hives was 12/1/21. My roommate was unaffected and I would get them no matter where I was (home vs school vs work). This made me determine that this was not caused by anything in my environment. The only way I was able to get any relief from the hives or itching was taking Benadryl. The itching/hives and Benadryl began to interfere with my daily functioning. I saw an allergist on 12/20/21. After an examination, he determined that I had excess mast cells in my skin which were releasing histamine, causing my hives. He demonstrated this through scratching my arm which immediately became red and raised. Fifteen minutes later, I developed hives on my neck/chest and opposite arm. It was at this time he postulated that this all was caused by my COVID booster shot which I received on 10/29/21, approximately 2 weeks before the itching began. He began me on an elimination diet, which consisted of no chocolate, nuts, alcohol, berries, or shellfish. I was also not allowed to take hot showers, was told to be gentle with my skin, and to take 1 Xyzal in the evening. After 2 weeks, he determined that the hives/itching were not caused by any food/drink but to continue with the Xyzal. At this time, I was not experiencing any hives/itching. The doctor told me on 2/7/22 to lessen my dosage to 1 pill every 2 days for 2 weeks and then 1 pill every 3 days for 2 weeks, then I wouldn?t take any at all. When I took the Xyzal every 2 days, the itching returned but it was tolerable. When I began taking it every 3 days, the itching began to interfere with my daily functioning once again. On 2/28/22, I was instructed to take the Xyzal every day once again to stop my itching and avoid the hives returning. This is where I am today.

symptom_text: Headache began around 8:30 PM and went from my temples and forehead to the base of my neck, followed a while later by pain in both arms between my shoulders and elbows.  Knowing sleep would be difficult, I stayed up until 2:00 AM and fell asleep about 3:00 AM.  I awoke at 3:20 AM trembling so badly that I couldn't hold a thermometer in my mouth.  So, it was time for "chills and fever" and I put sweat pants and a sweat shirt over my flannel Pjs, heavy socks on my feet, and socks on my hands.  My entire body felt ice cold.  Back under the covers, I finally warmed up and slept off and on for almost eight hours.Woke up around noon on Saturday, feverish, feeling nauseous, exhausted, and still feeling the headache and arm pains.  My "normal" temperature runs from 97.1 to 97.6, but ranged from 100.2 to 100.5 for two days after the vaccine.  Slept off and on around the clock on Saturday and Sunday, and by Monday the headache, pain, and fever were gone.  Slight nausea remained as well as the fatigue on Monday.  On Tuesday, my legs felt wobbly, like "sea legs."  By Wednesday, I was back to normal catching up on email and reading my books, and on Thursday drove out to the county to bring food to my sister and fix her PC.  I understand that seniors do not usually get the side effects as I did, because the immune system declines with age.  Apparently, my immune system is not aware of my birth date.  Can't help but wonder if taking Co-Q-10, as I've done for almost twenty-four years, has anything to do with it.

On 4/7/21, she received the second dose of the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine. Then, around 5/1/21, she developed fevers to 102 with associated fatigue and poor appetite, but no other clear localizing symptoms, including no sore throat, cough, chest pain, SOB, abdominal pain, N/V/D, joint swelling/pain, rashes, or dysuria. She presented to an outside hospital ED where she had an infectious workup that included a CXR concerning for LLL pneumonia. She was prescribed doxycycline for 7 days with resolution of her fevers and subjective improvement.    In early June 2021,  the patient redeveloped fevers and chills, worst at nighttime, without localizing symptoms. Her appetite and energy level remained very poor despite several changes to antidepressants as an outpatient. She was treated with nitrofurantoin x 5 days for presumed UTI, but fevers persisted, still without associated cough, CP, or SOB. With going fevers, fatigue, and poor appetite resulting in ~18lb unintentional weight loss, she was admitted to Hospital on 6/22/21 for further evaluation.  While at Hospital, she continued to have fevers to 102+ without localizing symptoms despite empiric doxycycline. A broad infectious workup returned negative. CT chest and CTAP were also unrevealing for a cause of fevers. She was found to have an elevated ferritin, LDH, and triglycerides, as well as a low fibrinogen, concerning for HLH (high H-score). She received high-dose dexamethasone. Bone marrow biopsy was performed that was negative for malignancy. However, peripheral flow cytometry returned with a clonal B-cell population, her soluble IL-2 was elevated, and she was found to have splenic enhancement on PET-CT, all concerning for occult lymphoma as the potential driver of her HLH. She remains admitted and is critically ill with complications of DIC and bleeding that preclude a splenic biopsy to confirm the suspected diagnosis of lymphoma. Since her fevers, malaise, and fatigue started less than 1 month after her second dose of the Moderna vaccine, and the patient was insistent that she "hadn't felt right" since she received that second dose of the vaccine, we decided to report this event in the VAERS system.

13 hours after injection, symptoms began. First, sudden onset of intense fever, followed by chills. Body temperature remained volatile for about 2-3 hours, switching between extreme hot and cold in intervals of 15 minutes or so. In addition, within the first 30 minutes of the initial fever, high levels of pain occurred from base of the skull down through neck, shoulders, upper back, and upper left arm (side that received injection). This pain was similar to muscular body aches you would have with a flu infection, but much more intense. Any attempt at movement was excruciating - I could not even move my arm or adjust positions without crying outloud or whimpering. Around 14 hours post-injection, a different kind of pain appeared: this seemed like a nerve problem of sorts. There was a sensation of pins and needles throughout my entire body, not just concentrated near the injection site. It was somewhat like the sensation we have when a limb "falls asleep" and produces tingling pain, but again, the intensity of the sensation was notable. The pins-and-needles, full-body nerve pain lasted for about 2 or 3 hours. The muscular pain that was concentrated around my neck, shoulders, and injection site lasted for about 5 hours, after which the arm that had received the injection was still very stiff and sore for the next day. However, the soreness in neck, shoulders, and upper back subsided after about 5 hours. The fever and chill cycles began to slow down after about 3 hours and stabilized within about 6 hours. I didn't attempt to treat any of the side effects, partly because I was immoblized by pain and fatigue, and partly because I wasn't sure if there were more effects to follow. The reaction began about 13 hours after receiving the vaccine, and with the exception of soreness at injection site, the symptoms resolved by about 18 hours post-injection.

symptom_text: Day of inoculation: [I note that the nurse didn't pull before injecting] Afternoon: heavy drowsiness and tiredness, arm soreness, no redness. Evening: fever (<40C), chills, worst malaise of my life, trembling, weakness, muscle aches all over the body, exhaustion, confusion, sleep disturbance, agitation. Frecuent urination. This lasted until day 3 post inoculation. There were feelings of depression in April in the morning, with oral temperature measurements slightly below 36 C, which I had never seen before (I take my oral temperature regularly: it goes from 36.4-5, to 37.5) even after mild exercise on a rebounder. This lasted a few (at least 3) days, then the morning low temperature disappeared.  On june 1 I wrote to my therapist about my pain on my forearms. I had been trying to hang in there with it, but now it was very frequent, and I used lidocaine cream that day. I was waking up tired and on pain often, with diffuse, mild body aches, and depression. I often felt a need to stretch in the morning, for my muscles (particularly my legs) felt stiff. On july 4 I woke up with strong diffuse body aches. I wanted to rush to the doctor, but realized I couldn't drive in such pain. It was Sunday. After about 1-2 hours the pain mostly subsided. I drove to an Urgent Care. My blood pressure was 144, over what I don't remember. My usual systolic is 120-125. We talked about my PTSD, aches and feelings of depression. He prescribed cyclobenzaprine 5mg, orally, every night. I asked for my blood pressure to be taken again. Now it was 158, over 91, I think (using a manual pump this time). I take the medication that night, the next day I feel much better, and my blood pressure was back to normal. July 25 I am emotionally unstable (from being well to sadness), with chest aches, frequent dissociation (depersonalization and derealization, but never sensory flashbacks), and sudden changes in energy levels, which I blame on having been recently triggered and hormonal changes. I have increasing trouble speaking, which I also blame on anxiety, despite it being far more than usual. At some point I go to health center, where it is dismissed as psychogenic. During august I keep waking up very tired, and now speech difficulties make fluent conversation practically impossible for most of my waking time: I know what I want to say, I understand language, I can read and write, but I cannot get my muscles to respond, or to respond at reasonable speeds. This starts happening to me for a couple of days after getting triggered (which didn't use to be that way) and then the problem kept showing up even when triggers were not involved. I get a sore throat, at take a picture of it. It is just reddened. I go to Health center, and request to be referred to a speech pathologist (the person, sadly, has been unreachable ever since). September: by mid september I am still waking up with stiff muscles, sore legs, feeling tired, and by september 14 (a few days after, I notice, I had several almost non-painful sores in my throat, which then disappeared before the other symptoms showed up) I am woken up numerous times by leg movements that involve dosiflexion of one of my feet at a time (usually my left), extension of the toes, fanning of the toes, and varying degrees of flexion of the knee, sometimes to the point of raising the leg to the height of the abdomen. This may happen 10 times a night. I start to feel scared. I try cyclobenzaprine 5mg for one night. It doesn't make a difference. Almost two weeks in I decide to try to find explanations for the phenomenon. At this point, I am experiencing trembling when I genuflect or kneel at church (a daily activity for years now), I need to use my hand to help myself get up, I still have trouble speaking early in the morning and late at night, and often forget words. I have trouble bringing my laundry basket up the steps i have to: my arms won't respond enough to attempt to raise the basket, even though  I can otherwise move them normally. I end up using my fingers as hooks and going up the steps walking backwards pushing with my legs. I lose the ability to put the recliner of the pew back into place with a flick of my foot as always, even though I can put it down (I don't have a vieo of the event, I think, but I did record a video later of what that motion is supposed to be like). By october 15 I had discovered the human plantar foot reflex, and tested mine following the example of doctors in social media repeatedly. The result was dorsiflexion of the foot, with raising of the big toe, fanning of the other toes, and flexion of the knee on my left leg, no response on my right leg. I have a video about that. It kept holding true on different days, using different objects to elicit the response. I also tried other "equivalent" reflex tests, with same results. I get reffered to a neurologist. Lowering my room temperature helps reduce the frequency of the episodes. I get a referral to a neurologist. About a week later, I accidentally discover something: upon stretching my neck diagonally as far as I can and looking forward again, my teeth chatter. This stops after I push my chin on my chest. It hapens bilaterally, and it is consistently repeatable. I update my doctor about it. I am terrified.  At this point my legs are often feeling sore, particularly my thigh (frontal part). I speak to my parish priest. He gievs me the annointment of the sick. My anxiety got muh better. I start taking a multivitamin for women that doesn't contain iron, looking for a good source of B vitamins. Over the next week, gradually, I had better nights, and symptom improvement, but the Babinski was still there, the leg contractions at night were still there (just not usually wasking me up after my bedroom temperature was moved from 74 to 70F) , an with that my leg trembling has disappeared. My attempt to perform the Romberg test resulted in lack of balance becoming evident. I spoke to a friend doctor, who asked me to stand on one leg. I would stand on my right leg properly, but not on my left (lose balance). OCtober:  I have been having  tender spots all over my body. I take pictures of my touching the sponts that hurt. I also have a mouth sore in my upper lip (picture taken). Sometime I went to urgent care and was told it was probably because I was sleeping so poorly. I was prescribed antidepressants, but I dnd't take them, because I wasn't feelng depressed, and I didn't want meds that carry suicide  thought risk. I also drew and took a picture of the drwaing representing painful areas My neurologist appointment came on nove 17. She reported to not having read my history because she couldn't understand my GPs handwriting. She repeated the Romberg test, my capacity to walk with one foot in foront of the other, both resulted with me losing balance. She looked for something in my eye, but said nothing.  She tested several of my deep tendon reflexes, without any reported findings. She asked me to run my heel pver my shins: that resulted in no respnse on my right leg, but in dorsiflexion of the foot and raising of the big toe and fanning of the toes in my left foot. The same when I asked her to test for a Babinski sign. She ordered a B12 measurement, a thyroid hormone measurement, and a ferriting measurement. My ferritin level was 4.4 (4 something, that's for sure), if I remember correctly, and I was avised to talk to my GP bout iron supplementation or infusions. I started taking 65mg of iron a day since the day after the appointment. All else was great. Since that very night my legs have been awakening me again (particularly my left) with the same moveements as before. I demonstrated the chatter to a psichatric nurse yesterday )I was volunteering for something), and this time the chattering didn't stop through the usual mechanisms. I have a recording of the chatttering the day I went to the neurologist and of yesterday. This time the chattering lasted more than 5 minutes. After it didn't stop the suual way, Ithe nurse recommended that I should record it, and so I did, for more than 5 minutes. The chattering didn't end by the end of the vieo, but it did stop eventually, maybe within 10 minutes of the start. This had never happened befor I also recor mysef eating during the episode, and speaking. The phenomenon doesn't make itdifficult to eat, or swallow, and is not painful. It doesn't feel like the chattering from cold, and can happen at any temperature. I haven't been successful at trying to trigger it while lying down. I can make it stop by tensing some different muscles, but it comes back if I relax my jaw during an episode. I noticed in the video that, even whenI stop it like this, my face doesn't look quite right. I also noticed that I blinked a lot, but I don't remember if the wind was causing that. It did make it difficul for me to speak at some point, which is evidenced in the video. The mechanisms that I used and work for me when I am having difficulty speaking due to anxiety had absolutely no effect in this case. I may note that the leg movements aren't only present while I sleep, but also when I am close to falling asleep. Also, that sometimes (occassionally) they involve a rather circular motion of the foot, resulting in the foot "climbimg" up the bed, flesing upwards, thento the left, then downard as if rgoing back to the neutral position, releatedly and wuickly in a successive motion about three times or two.. Also that the contractions last a few seconds. I don't feel that I have any control over the foot during those moments. Another note, which I don't know how relevant it may be, is that I shiver very strongly:my whole back sways, my butt moves widely, my head goes out of position, and I have never seen anyone shiver like that. It hasn't always been this way, but I don't remember how long this has been. My doctor, listed here, I think, was not at the Health center when I had the severe and almost constant difficulty speaking. My academic advisor has seen it. A lot of the content of this long text has been based, not only on memory, but on writings that I directed to my therapist or friends reporting to her what was going on soon after the events took place, so when dates are stated or numbers are given they are accurate unless doubt is expressed, to  the best of my ability. I would be happy to make the videos available to you, also, if you may find them to be of help. I also had some headaches during october, but don't remember the dates. They were migraine-like, but not very intense 9except, sometimes, for a few seconds), no nausea or dizziness, or fainting, or loss of consciousness.. At some point, on a few days, I also tried using the rebounder to try to regain a bit of balance and muscle strength. I am a female, virgin, no contraceptives ever, no smoker nor do I consume any other drug, except as described, I am 5'3", 157 pounds by now (my weight has been increasing, but not suspisciously quickly). I had anemia last year due to iron deficiency, but had been corrected before. I have heavy period, which may explain, current low iron levels.

symptom_text: It was May 16 in the afternoon. I was feeling just very unenergetic. Temperature was hardly up at all. I'm normally low, my temperature is usually 97.7. it went up to 98 around there. It wasn't bad temperature wise. I noticed I was getting a lot of nasal congestion and just no energy. With the nasal congestion, I was thinking of the smoke from the wild fires. That's why I didn't do testing right away. As the afternoon went on, I started feeling no energy at all and started developing a cough. I had the nasal congestion and cough that were my first indicators. I had no temp change. I took the at home test and it was positive and isolated to the guest bedroom. Wore a mask around the house. It went on like that, felt like I got hit by a truck with no energy. That continued and I was basically in bed because I was tired and couldn't do much. Kept eating normally but wasn't too hungry. I noticed that all of a sudden, when I ate, I couldn't tell what I was eating. Lost my taste and smell, and that's slowly coming back. On May 18, I called Dr. and we set up an appointment online in the afternoon. He listened to my symptoms and he wasn't too worried about me. We went over the check sheet for qualification for medication. He said I was doing fine and I wouldn't be eligible for the antiviral pill. I waited it out and said I'd get back with him Friday. Friday the 20th, my wife went in to a HCF and came back negative. They called me and said to come in to take a test in the afternoon. It was a rapid test and it came back positive. I got an interview with a doctor and she recommended the Paxlovid. She sent a prescription in and I picked that up later that day. Started taking it immediately that evening. 3 in the evening and in the morning for 5 days. I started that the evening of the 20th and finished the morning of the 25th. It wasn't miraculous. It didn't cure me over a day or two, but things started to get better. On the 25th, I finished that up. And I was up a lot more, wasn't in bed as much like the previous week. I was able to venture out with my mask on. I tried to get another test on the 5/27 but they were booked and said they could take me in on the 28th. I went in, got retested and this came back negative. Happy with that. 4PM on 5/28 was the negative test. Just been careful and wearing a mask since. At the moment, I'm doing better. I'm not real active right now, but will try to get myself going again next week. Congestion has moved from nasal passages to chest during the COVID time period, a little bit of congestion left in chest. Currently in recovery.

On Friday, 12/1/23, at the clinic we had a 7-month pregnant woman from another country faint.  I had immunized her with a Spikevax vaccine a few hours prior to her fainting.  I can't be exact on the time frame but it was definitely hours later.  I'm not sure why she hung around the clinic for such a long time but I think it's because she was waiting for her partner to get vaccinated and he wasn't in line with her.  He must have arrived later.  There was lots going on of course so I wasn't paying specific attention to her but I was aware that she was hanging around the room with other migrants.  She was sitting in a chair in the back corner of the room and all of a sudden there was commotion in her direction.  I noticed her partner was fanning her and someone else was talking to her.   I ran over to her to see what was happening and realized she was going to pass out. She was sweaty and shaking and eventually passed out.  I just supported her body, put her legs up on a chair and called for someone to bring the medical bag.  There was a Medical Assistant at the clinic too, I don't know who she works for or her name, but she ran over first with a blood pressure cuff and glucose testing strips.  When the woman came to, she vomited into a garbage can.  Her blood pressure was low but not alarmingly low, I don't remember her specific BP numbers.  Her blood sugar was 78.    In the meantime, someone called emergency services and relayed all the information we had.  With the help of an interpreter, we were able to assess that the woman hadn't eaten all day except for some fruit in the morning so we were able to give her some juice and a cookie however a few minutes later she vomited again.  I believe she fainted because of not eating right that day and the stress her body was under with her travels to this country and her pregnancy not because of the vaccine.  When the paramedics arrived, I let them take over her care.  She refused to be taken to the hospital for further care and signed a document with the paramedics to that effect.

symptom_text: Within the first 10 minutes of receiving the vaccine, my heart started racing and I began to feel dizzy and lightheaded. I am an athlete and am used to fast cardio, racing heart, but this was not like anything I had ever felt before. I had difficulty located a nurse to help me. When someone finally saw I needed help, the nurse came over and took my blood pressure and pulse. She said my pulse was abnormally high as was my blood pressure and that I looked bad. She told me to take deep breaths and asked if it were a panic attack. I said it was not. I was able to control my breathing and stay calm and I eventually my heart rate came down. She did not offer me a place to lay down even though I felt like passing out. She told me that I should sit a little longer. Within another 10 minutes the same exact reaction happened again. At this point I told her I was a little worried as I've never had this kind of reaction before. She then took my bloood pressure and pulse again and told me to deep breathe. The pulse and blood pressure eventually came down. She asked me if I wanted water. I had water and some trail mix that I happen to have on me. I had to use the restroom, she walked me to the restroom. Once I realized I was not going to be offered any additional care, I decided to try and drive home. By the time I was home those symptoms had subsided, but I had a terrible migraine headache (Friday night). I went to bed and woke up the next morning with a small headache (Saturday morning). The migraine came back that night along with intense arm pain. The next morning (Sunday morning) after that I felt better and then later that night the migraine came back. On Monday those symptoms had subsided. I seemed to be getting better, but on Friday, January 22 (one week after the initial vaccine) my arm was burning and swollen and itched a lot. The injection site was warm to the touch and very tender. The swelling lasted until Sunday, January 24th. I finally called my physician on Monday, January 25th. I wasn't sure if I should get the second dose or not. Her nurse called me back and told me that my symptoms were not normal and that if I wanted to get the second dose I could take Benadryl ahead of time. I have not taken the second dose at this point.  Today, January 27th, my arm seems to be better, but occasionally itches and I feel a sharp pain sometimes at random. My second dose is scheduled for February 12, 2021.

On June, 9, 2021, the day after I received the 2nd dose of the Moderna vaccine, I experienced intense pain in my left arm.  I expected pain in my arm again since that is how it felt the first time.  The pain felt as if someone punched me extremely hard, leaving me feeling like I needed a sling to support the injury.  The pain in my left arm felt had a throbbing, pulsing, almost numbing feel all on the outside and although it did feel a little different than the first time, I figured it would get better like after the first vaccine I received on May 11, 2021.   Other symptoms I experienced were: waxing and waning low-grade fevers all day, severe fatigue and brain fog, dizziness,  little appetite, shakiness, rapid breathing and then shallow breathing (in line with my heart pounding or slowing down), and nausea. The symptoms were familiar to me, and it felt like deja vu but a milder version of when I had Covid-19 in August 2020.  As a reference to what I will mention next, when I had Covid-19 last year I developed subacute thyroiditis from the acute respiratory virus, and this was supported by a blood test.  My levels appeared to be normal going into the vaccine, and since I never have had thyroid challenges the past I didn't expect to have fluctuating hormones post Covid or post-vaccine.   As of now, July 14, 2021, I still am experiencing some of the milder symptoms on occasion (brain fog, dizziness, shakiness), and the hormone regulation has been a bit off too.  My left arm has a dull ache/pain and numbness the starts at the vaccine site in my shoulder down the outside of the arm, pulses pain in my left wrist, and stops at the last two fingers on my left hand.  As far as I can tell, I do have full range of motion and can still exercise.  My recovery time is slower and the tingling feeling doesn't subside, and if anything it increases randomly.  I was hoping the dull ache and numb feeling would subside by this point, but it hasn't.  My best guess is that I have neurological damage in my left arm, and I have a long term recovery in my hormonal health.

I had already dealt with chronic pain, but this wasn't normal for me, so I called the doctor. She told me to wait a few more days and to come to the clinic if it didn't subside. During these three weeks, not only did I have leg pain and a sore injection site, but I also felt extreme malaise and weakness. I now wonder if the interaction of the vaccine and methylprednisolone exacerbated the inflammation.

After the 15 minute waiting period, I felt fine. I did my grocery shopping while I was at the store, went home and worked the rest of the day at my desk. We ran errands in the evening like normal. I hadn't really noticed because we were busy, but my heart rate had been steadily increasing all afternoon and into the evening. My watch tracks my pulse rate and reports on screen. After I took a shower at 9:30, I noticed that my pulse felt high. I laid down, thinking it was just from taking a hot shower and it would go back down to normal.  That's when I looked at my watch report and it looked like a stair step, with my heart rate increasing steadily every few hours, starting at 4 p.m. It was currently 110-120 (my normal RHR is 60, and drops into the 50s when I'm asleep). I went to bed, hoping I was just in my own head about this and it would be fine. I woke at 2 a.m.  and my heart rate had not dropped below 100 while I was asleep and was at 130. I went to the ER at 2:00 a.m. because it was alarming. There were points where it spiked to 150 while sitting still. The ER ran an EKG, full blood and urine labs, monitored my heart rate and BP - my BP was in the normal range the whole time. The doctor who saw me in the ER was awesome. Her husband is still dealing with lingering neurological damage from having COVID last year. She informed me that I was not in a-fib or any type of cardiac distress and my labs were all normal, but was likely having an immune response to the vaccine.  They did a chest x-ray and CT to check for blood clots and both came back negative. My platelet count was well within normal range as well. I returned home about 6 a.m.  and my heart rate was still higher than normal, but had already started to work its way down. It stair-stepped down just like it went up and by 4 p.m., my RHR was back down to 70 and it was down in the 50s overnight. Aside from that, I had the typical headache, low-grade temp and overall body aches. Everything had subsided by Sunday afternoon. I did make an appointment see my PCP as instructed by the ER doctor on Tuesday, April 13. She had read all reports from the ER and was pleased with how my heart rate had come back down to normal. This was the same day that the authorities stopped use of the Jannsen shot due to the blood clot concerns. Dr ran another platelet count for my own peace of mind and it was a little higher than it was when I was in the ER, so she was confident that I was not in any danger, but did review the symptoms/warning signs of blood clots with me just in case.  I have not had any issues or symptoms since.

Sunday, I felt a little bit better but energy was still low - unusual tiredness; couldn't exercise as I felt a heavy fatigue. On Sunday, I went to a dance class but it was difficult as I was tired. On Monday, I felt a tiny bit better but still fatigued and did another dance class which went a little better. On Monday evening, I felt like I did the night of the injection - a little loopy and "drunk like." Monday night, I woke up with a Fiery, achy, itchy, burning rash on both of my arms and the tops of my legs. If I would itch it, it would exaggerate it. When I woke up the next day - the rash went everywhere in my body - it would come and go in different places - neck, face, down and up my legs and feet and on my butt. Pretty much every spot had the rash at one time or another. It was really bad on Tuesday morning, I called the doctor. Was treated with Benadryl and cortisone cream which helped with the symptoms. Tuesday night, it was excruciating - it was all up and down my legs, arms, neck and face and stomach and rear end and feet. It was very achy, burning and itchy - very intense. It would hurt if I scratched it. Accompanied with really intense fatigue. Wednesday, after taking Benadryl, I woke up and it was a tiny bit better. It was still on my legs, neck and face. Saturday, it was pretty much gone but it would threaten to come back and I felt itchiness in my legs when I went for a walk. It still feels a little lingering - my legs are itchy. I'm still building back my energy. Incrementally my energy is increasing. Still not 100% there but it's getting better day by day.  Note: My history with my skin: I do get flare ups when I get bug bites and when I get poison ivy - I have very sensitive skin.

Both he and she were extensively counseled regarding signs and symptoms to be on the lookout for that would indicate the need for further medical evaluation and they both expressed complete understanding and agreement. symptom_text: I received the shot on Friday, June 25 at about 1630 hours. At about 1500 the next day, Saturday, June 26, I felt a fever coming on. By the next morning it had dissipated, and other than a sore arm and some general fatigue, I felt better. I went to work all the next week, but on Saturday, July 3rd, I slept until almost noon, which is very unusual for me; also I awoke with a bloody nose. The only thing of note during the week was that my right calf and thigh started hurting in a couple of places, but I figured that I must have strained it slightly and that the pain would go away soon. I did take some naproxen during the week and it seemed to help.  I started doing some yard work and as I was mowing I felt like it was getting hard to breathe. I finished the front lawn, which is not very big, and sat down for about a half-hour and rested before tackling the back. Usually I do the whole thing at once and it doesn't take me very long. I found that as I mowed the rest of the lawn that I was really struggling to breathe and I couldn't take a deep breath at all. I felt like I was going to collapse but i managed to make it back inside and sit down. I must have sat for a couple of hours before laying on the couch in search of a place where I felt like I could take a breath. I didn't feel like I could pull in all the air that I wanted to, no matter how hard I tried. After about four hours I got up and went to bed, where I slept for about 12 hours and again awoke with a bloody nose. I basically spent all of Sunday, July 4 and Monday, July 5 in a recliner resting and trying to breathe. My right leg was still hurting and I still couldn't draw a complete breath.  I made myself get up and go to work on Tuesday, July 6, and made it through despite having to stop and gasp following every exertion (even walking a few feet). I took more naproxen and pushed through the rest of the week, having decided that maybe I had a touch of pneumonia and that maybe it was getting better. My right leg continued to hurt and I still couldn't take anything resembling a deep breath, no matter how much i wanted to. On Saturday, July 10, I laid down on the couch in the early afternoon and passed out for several hours. My wife, who had been out of town for most of the prior week (else I would no doubt have been to the ER sooner) got worried and checked my temperature and O2 levels and found my oxygen to be low and my temperature to be high. She insisted that we go to the emergency room. We went, and following an EKG, a CT scan, an X-ray, and an ultrasound I was diagnosed with multiple bilateral pulmonary embolisms and was admitted into the hospital on July 11, 2021. I started a course of Eliquis and as I was responding well in terms of no pain and having passed an echocardiogram, I was discharged at about 1700 on July 11. I have been on Eliquis since, and have had two follow-ups with my PCP as well as two different blood work done, both of which show improvement. I also have an appointment with the hematology clinic  on August 17. I am feeling better now, can breathe easier now, and do not have as much fatigue as my stamina returns. My right leg does not hurt any longer and the swelling is mostly gone.

symptom_text: Patient was healthy and well until she received the J&J vaccine May 5, 2021. No immediate reactions were noted until May 17, 2021 when she noted edema of her legs L>R. She actively run 5 and 10 K races without dyspnea or pain at the time and denied leg pain. One May 25, she came home for a medical exam; Edema was noted but no heart, lung  abnormalities were found or leg tenderness was absent. A Doppler sonogram of the legs and MRI of the knees were normal.   In late July, 2021 Patient experienced auditory, taste and visual hallucinations. She seemed agitated and talked incessantly. She expressed delusional ideation to her parents when she visited them  August 1-5, 2021. To her mother, a Child Neurologist, she appeared confused, anxious, with a severe tachycardia, dilated pupils, warm erythematous extremities and sweaty palms. In a local ER she had a normal Brain CT, TSH, Lyme, CBC and CMP. She expressed fear that her family might harm her. She was transported to a larger Hospital. During the trip she experienced frequent urination without dysuria, anorexia. She described early satiety and described a prior seven days of eating only flavored water. Complaints of thirst with habitual water drinking and polyuria occurred in late July and continued into her September psych hospitalization but would resolve when tests at the hospital required prolonged fasting. She developed constipation going 7-10 days with no bowel movement. During a 7 day hospitalization she was grossly psychotic. These episodes markedly worsened with in 15-45 minutes of eating a meal. Grossly feculent breath was noted after many meals but seemed to clear a 4-5 hours. In addition she demonstrated severe and recurrent postural tachycardia, incompletely improved by IV saline?s c/w Potts syndrome. 48 hour cardiac monitor revealed recurrent sinus tachycardia. Head MRI, CXR, CMP, CBCd, EEG, Chest and Abd CT, and lumbar puncture were normal. Multiple CNS markers for limbic encephalitis were absent. Attempts at longer term psychiatric hospitalization failed due to unavailable beds for admission. After multiple threats of self harm and continued paranoid ideation she was admitted to Psychiatric Hospital. She was given Seroquel but became angry and irritable. It was discontinued after 8 days.  A prior Lactulose Breath Test returned very positive and c/w  small bowel bacterial overgrowth. This prompted the start of Xifaxin 550 mgm tid. Simultaneously, a she was started on Lithium carbonate 300 mgm bid after a diagnosis of bipolar disorder manic type was made by multiple Psychiatry consultants. Within 48 hours of these two therapies, her affect and ideation returned to normal. No further hallucinations were noted. She expressed clear awareness of her prior hallucinations and faulty ideation.  Xifaxin was tapered to daily in November and stopped completely by 02/01/2022. Bid Lithium carbonate continues yielding low therapeutic blood levels of Lithium.  Several consultants believe that Patient developed a dysautonomia of the autonomic nervous system, i.e.,Gillian-Barre dysautonomia (Pott?s Syndrome, gastroparesis, small bowel bacterial overgrowth, hypomotility of the small and large bowel, and peripheral sympathetic dystrophy) and early limbic encephalitis with psychosis, manic type and that this followed the J&J vaccine. She remains clinically normal except for recurrent  asymmetric edema. of the L lower extremity.

As I examined it further, I realized that this mass was not there previously and warning shots fired off in my head, immediately. I immediately asked my grandmother to do another examination of my breast, and she confirmed my suspicion that there was a foreign mass located above my nipple in my left breast. It was difficult for me to closely monitor this mass as it was difficult for me to think about it as it triggered emotional distress. I asked my mom to do an examination and she also noted the mass. A little more than a week later, I noticed that the mass shrunk. Since everyone in my family was on edge for nearly a week suspecting that a 21 year old female in their family could possibly have breast cancer, this caused my family to consult my grandmother?s doctor, and have her assistant contact me about what could potentially be happening. Her assistant spoke to me over the phone and communicated that it is important for me to have the mass formally examined and for me to receive a mammogram. She also mentioned that many women who have received the vaccine also noticed irregular lumps in their breasts after receiving the vaccine. I want women in my age range to be aware that they might notice lumps in their breasts after the vaccine and not to experience the same emotional distress of thinking that they have breast cancer when it could be inflammation occurring in their lymph nodes as a result of being administered the Covid vaccine.
