From admission H&P dated 9/12/21 by Doctor: "History per chart and collateral given patient's encephalopathy. The patient was reportedly in USOH when she began experiencing abdominal pain. She reportedly started a short course of penicillin as an outpatient for this abdominal pain. She presented to the Hospital with worsening abdominal pain, worsening of her chronic low back pain, and chest pain. Mild leukocytosis with elevated ALT and bilirubin on admission. Troponin was elevated to 0.44, but down-trended and deemed to be non-cardiac after evaluation by cardiology. CXR, UA not concerning for infection. CT-AP showed diffuse colonic wall thickening, mild pulmonary interstitial opacities, small bilateral pleural effusions, and a horseshoe kidney. V/Q scan without PE, ultrasound of LE showed patents. TTE with normal EF, RUQUS without biliary dilation, only mild fatty infiltration of the liver. Stool-filled colon - had pain relief with aggressive bowel regimen and bowel movement.    Due to persistent fevers and back pain with elevated procalcitonin, the patient was started empirically on ceftriaxone and vancomycin. Negative CT-spine for infection.   Course complicated by 2x episodes of afib with RVR, the second one requiring amiodarone and beta blocker. She also developed an AKI with Cr rising to peak of 3.56 over the course of days. Intermittent hypotension requiring pressors. Renal consulted, workup concerning for glomerulonephritis, revealed hypocomplementemia, ferritin >80,000, and monoclonal IgG kappa. She refused a bone marrow biopsy. Her urine output dropped to near-anuric, and she became encephalopathic with myoclonus. At this point, she was started on every other day dialysis. No head imaging performed.   Other diagnostic studies included utox (positive for morphine and oxycodone), APAP level (undetectible), Hep C, HepB, C.Diff,    Due to the elevated ferritin and concern for HLH, he was evaluated by hematology, started on dexamethasone. She had hypoxemic respiratory failure requiring bipap that was ultimately weaned to nasal cannula.   Past medical history of major depressive disorder and chronic lower back pain. Notably, she had severe osteomyeletis of the LUE, LLE requiring extensive surgery"   HOSPITAL COURSE:  Patient had an unfortunately complicated hospital course. As above, she was transferred from an outside facility with a constellation of clinical and lab abnormalities including fever of unknown origin, abdominal/chest pain, anuric renal failure requiring iHD, respiratory failure, and encephalopathy as well as cryoglobulinemia, hypocomplementemia and hyperferritniemia (>80K) and developing bicytopenia with concern for, though not diagnosis of, HLH from unclear trigger.  While pursuing workup for unifying diagnosis she developed progressive multiorgan failure as will be discussed below. In regards to diagnostics for underlying diagnosis, with the assistance of multiple consulting services (infectious diseases, heme/onc, rheumatology, nephrology) she underwent broad workup for diagnosis of and trigger of HLH v. Alternative inflammatory/rheumatologic process including bone marrow biopsy (in progress) , rheumatologic workup (notable for low complement levels and reported cryoglobulinemia at OSH), infectious workup via blood/BAL/LP (negative/in progress). Realization that cryoglobulins + at OSH as well as development of chest/abdomen rash and discolored toes raised question of cryoblobulinemic vasculitis. She was empirically treated with 1g IV methylpred then 40mg IV dex/day while awaiting results and diagnostics which unfortunately were not complete prior to her death and remains a question, hopefully to be answered by pending autopsy. Despite gradual improvement in several body systems (hemodynamics, hypoxemia), she developed DIC and pulmonary hemorrhage on the day of her death which ultimately led to her death as described below.    Multiorgan failure will be described below by system:  # Hypoxemic respiratory failure: Intubated for airway protection and hypoxemia upon admission to UWMC. Treated for ARDS with LPV possibly secondary to infection, though notably BAL and other infectious workup remained unremarkable throughout her stay. Hypoxemia improved enough with UF for volume removal and empiric ABX to move towards SBT pt was not able to be extubated. On the day of Patient's death, she developed bloody secretions from ETT so underwent repeat bronchoscopy. BAL diagnostic of alveolar hemorrhage with progressively bloody lavage aliquots. She was re-pulsed with IV methylpred and provided platelet replacement with concern for DAH or pulmonary vasculitis on 9/17 though developed severe pulmonary hemorrhage early on 9/18. Despite MTP and DDAVP to try and stabilize coagulopathy/hemorrhage, she ultimately lost >3L blood from ETT and died following this significant pulmonary hemorrhage (see code note and death note from today's date).    # Shock: Developed distributive shock requiring 3 vasopressors for support early in her stay. She received empiric antimicrobials, high dose steroids and ID workup with no revealing cause for sepsis. Hemodynamics showed signs of improvement leading up to day of death with vasopressors nearly weaned off.    #anuric renal failure- Complicated by anascarca, hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis. By microscopy related to tubular injury, considered possibly related to cryoglobulinemia v. Vasculitis though unable to pursue renal biopsy due to instability. Required intermittent SLED/SCUF while admitted.    # Encephalopathy: Again, unclear etiology of altered mental status. Initially considered related to sedation and metabolic abnormalities and initial CT head WNL and LP without clear infectious cause (though some studies remain in progress), though remained profoundly encephalopathic following wean of sedatives.  Other considerations have included CNS involvement of primary underlying diagnosis (cryoglobulinemic vasculitis), undiagnosed infection, NCSE, etc.    # DIC # Bicytopenia Likely related to underlying unifying diagnosis. Other considerations included MAHA though no evidence of hemolysis, negative HIT assay, HLH.  Progressive throughout stay requiring cryo transfusion and multiple PLT transfusions on day of death.

In the ED, patient was found to be saturating in the 90s on room air.  He did get up to walk and his saturations dropped to approximately 88. He was also slightly hypertensive to 157/108.  His respiratory rate was also slightly elevated in the 20s.  His lab workup was notable for an ESR of 25, a CRP 8.2, and a D-dimer of 0.92.  There was no leukocytosis or electrolyte abnormalities and troponin was negative at less than 0.01.  CT chest showed no evidence of pulmonary embolism.  There was scattered bilateral areas of airspace disease in all 5 lobes consistent with a viral pneumonia.  He received a DuoNeb treatment, azithromycin, Rocephin, and a dose of Solu-Medrol 125 mg. He was subsequently admitted to our service for management of COVID-19 infection.  10/26/21: Patient is a 52-year-old gentleman with history significant for gout who presented to the ED with worsening shortness of breath, cough, and fatigue for the last several days.  Patient tested positive for COVID-19 approximately 6 days prior to admission.  He did receive the Johnson Johnson vaccine several months ago.  At time of admission he had been symptomatic for 11 days.  In the ED, he was found to be hypoxic with walk test, he was started on supplemental oxygen.  D-dimer was 0.92, CTA chest showed no evidence of pulmonary embolism.  CT findings were consistent with viral pneumonia.  Due to need for supplemental oxygen patient was treated with remdesivir and dexamethasone.  Due to elevated D-dimer he was also started on prophylactic Lovenox daily. He did not need further treatment with remdesivir dexamethasone, VTE risk factor score did not qualify him for home anticoagulation. He is to follow-up with his PCP.

I basically slept most of day Sunday ; This time in my room with  3 blankets (light blankets )and heat up (felt like 80°F under blankets). I was sweating under the blankets but it really helped warm me up and alleviate my chills. I woke up later that day to a call to help my sister with some work. MYCOPLASMA PNEUMONIA; This spontaneous report was received from other health professional via literature:  This report concerned a 66 year old female of an unspecified race and ethnicity. The objective of this study was to test a series of sputa and nasopharyngeal swabs collected in patients with upper respiratory symptoms for infection by Mycoplasma pneumonia as well as SARS-CoV2 (severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2) using in situ based methods and then to correlate the results with the clinical information. The patient's height, and weight were not reported. The patient's pre-existing medical conditions included: Patient was in good health before vaccination. The patient received covid-19 vaccine ad26.cov2.s (suspension for injection, route of admin, batch number and expiry date were not reported) dose, start therapy date were not reported, 1 total administered for covid-19 prophylaxis. The batch number was not reported. Per procedure, no follow-up will be requested for this case. Age at time of vaccination 7 decade old. No concomitant medications were reported.  On an unspecified date in early DEC-2022, patient had worsening upper respiratory symptoms with abundant mucous production including sinusitis, and an incessant cough. Patient had a low grade fever 38.2 degree Celsius and had complained of a persistent cough with no respiratory distress. The samples were each tested for SARS-CoV2 (severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2) by qRTPCR (Quantitative Reverse Transcription polymerase chain reaction) and scored as negative or positive. Patient was tested negative for SARS-CoV2 by qRTPCR. Patient had abundant mucous production with clear sputa which was retrieved and samples placed on glass slides for in situ based testing. The patient had chest X-ray and diagnosed as negative for pneumonia. A review of the cytologic features of the nasopharygeal swabs and sputa was done after hematoxylin and eosin staining. The SARS-CoV2 negative cytology showed an admixture of normal glandular cells in clusters amongst bland squamous cells with scattered mononuclear cells. In comparison, to the SARS-CoV2 positive cytology specimens which showed extensive degenerative changes in the glandular cells. The degenerative changes were evidenced as nuclear enlargement, degeneration, and cytolysis. Inflammatory cells were present, typically evidenced as mononuclear cells/macrophages with rare neutrophils and eosinophils. In comparison, the patient was ultimately diagnosed as Mycoplasma pneumonia likewise showed degenerated glandular cells. However, though mononuclear cells were evident, there were relatively more neutrophils. Further, mucous was abundant. Immunohistochemistry was next done for SARS-CoV2 spike protein (both S1 and S2 subunits) and RSV (respiratory syncytial virus) proteins blinded to the clinical and viral information. Patient was negative for both SARS-CoV2 spike protein and RSV. In situ hybridization was done for adenovirus and Mycoplasma pneumonia DNA. An abundant Mycoplasma pneumonia was detected by in situ hybridization. Note that the signal was intense, consistent with large amounts of bacteria, and localized in discrete packets in cells with the cytologic features of macrophages. Patient was treated with doxycycline (100 mg twice a day (BID) for 7 days). The patient's symptoms began to resolve, though not completely, soon after antibiotic therapy was begun. Patient had repeat nasopharyngeal swabs and sputa tested for Mycoplasma pneumonia five days after the onset of antibiotic therapy and there was no Mycoplasma pneumonia were noted by in situ hybridization. The action taken with covid-19 vaccine ad26.cov2.s was not applicable. The patient was recovering from mycoplasma pneumonia. The authors concluded that other pathogens that were well documented to be able to cause upper respiratory diseases include influenza A, B, RSV, and Mycoplasma pneumonia. Although vaccines were now routinely available for SARS-CoV2 and influenza A, mild infections could still occur in people who had been vaccinated. In situ hybridization for Mycoplasma pneumonia was strongly positive in the present case. The patients were given doxycycline and five days later each sputa/nasopharygeal swab was negative for Mycoplasma pneumonia by in situ hybridization. Hence rapid diagnosis could lead to antibiotic therapy which had been shown to shorten the time period of symptoms which can be clinically problematic with this disease. This report was serious (Other Medically Important Condition). symptom_text: Around 5:00 PM after having gotten my shot, I arrived home from a drive down to meet my sister. Precautions were taken, masks were worn, safe social distance was maintained and I have no reason to believe any of the symptoms I experienced upon returning home were related to anything other than the vaccine, particularly since first that is how vaccines work and second one of my friends who was vaccinated at the same time as me at the clinic was going through similar pains.  It started as a discomfort in my intestines or possibly just below my stomach in general. I thought my pants were too tight but just in case I let my mom take over driving the rest of the way home. When I got to the house, I had about an hour of usable time left before I went into a complete state of delirium. We're not sure how high my fever actually got before my mom woke up and checked in on me at 9:00 PM, but after having pulled the covers away I registered at 102.5° F. I was screaming in a half-awake and half-asleep nightmare, trying to get someone to come help me and unable to get anyone's attention. I would, as a result, like to insist that it be added to recommendations to not be alone after getting the vaccine! For the whole first night! I believe that I genuinely could have died. My brain was melting for lack of more proper medical terminology, and I stopped being able to understand and speak my own first language in an incredibly confused state. This was entirely a result of two simultaneous factors: Fever and Chills. First, the fever made my skin ache. Wearing any clothing hurt. But once I took off my pants in exchange for some breezy shorts, I was covered in goosebumps and feeling frozen even though it was solidly in the 70s. I claimed under blankets and still couldn't get warm enough. The backs of my thighs were insanely hot in comparison to the fronts of them, so I just warmed my body under 3 layers of blankets trying to get the chills to go away. I did that for about four hours during which time I was basically constantly screaming incoherently.

In Dec. of 2020 I tested positive for having COVID-19 by a nasal swab and experienced mild flu like symptoms. On April 12, 2021, I received the J&J Covid-19 Vaccine. The next day I experienced the worst headache I have ever experienced, with splitting head pain for 7+ hours. The following few days I experienced mild fatigue. On May 3rd, 2021 while at work I noticed what I thought was a floater in my right eye. Over the next few days, the floater was still present and I randomly would experience mild pressure behind my right eye. After doing my own eye tests, I quickly realized that it wasn't a floater rather I had lost vision in the lower left part of my peripheral vision in my right eye. Since it didn't limit my activities of daily living, I waited until I had my annual wellness exam on 5/25/21 with my PCP, Dr. at Health. Dr. recommended that I see an Optometrist (please note at this visit I was overdue for my Tdap vaccine and Dr. recommended that I receive this vaccine, which I did). On 6/3/21 I saw Dr., OD at  Eye Care Center. Dr.  noted that I had swelling around my optic nerve in my right eye and had hemorrhages in the back of my eye. She scheduled a follow up and ordered blood work and eventually after another follow up, an MRI of my head and eye. Everything checked out okay and it was at this point that Dr. believed I had, ?Non-Arteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy?. She referred me to see a Neuro-Opthamologist at Health Center. On 7/29/21 I saw Dr., MD and after his examination he believed I did have?Non-Arteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy?. It was his opinion that this was an uncommon condition for someone my age but that I do have risk factors, including a small optic cup, and a history of obstructive sleep apnea (which I am compliant in CPAP therapy since being diagnosed). I was also recently found to have hyperlipidemia with a high LDL cholesterol level (137 on 6/4/21) and also have prediabetes with a slightly elevated hemoglobin A1c (5.8 on 5/25/21). When asked if this could have been a result of receiving the J&J vaccine less than 30 days prior to experiencing my vision loss, he didn?t feel that there was a correlation however that everything about this vaccine is new.  When asked if I should report this event, he stated he did not think there was a relation but he supported my preference to do so.  I am only reporting this not because I absolutely believe the vaccine caused this problem in my eye, but I do have some concerns that it may have contributed to this. I can?t stress enough how horrendous the headache was the next day after receiving the vaccine and with already having covid antibodies in my system at vaccine time, I am concerned about the possibility of this happening to my eye due to the vaccine.  I have no prior history of eye diseases or problems (minus an occasional sty) and have no family history of eye problems either. I am only reporting this in hopes that IF there could be a possible safety concern that I can be part of the solution to making sure these vaccines are safe for everyone going forward.

symptom_text: Client received the COVID vaccine Janssen Lot#205A21A at 1:29 PM. RN was alerted by the client's family prior to vaccination that the client has a history of "fainting" with injections. RN recommended vaccination on the cot in the observation area to decrease risk of syncope. The client and his parents refused vaccination in the observation area and his mother stated "if he can look at his phone he'll be fine." The client received the vaccination at the table and ambulated to the observation area. RN was alerted by the client's parents at 1:39 and responded. EMT also responded at this time. The client was not verbally responsive to RN and EMT and his posture was tense sitting in the chair. RN elevated the client's legs on a metal chair. The client's posture relaxed and subsequently the client regained responsiveness. No injury was sustained. The client then stated that he was dizzy and lightheaded. He denied SOB, throat tightening, and itching. . Client was AOx4. Vitals obtained by EMT were as follows: BP 132/88 and HR 64 regular rate and rhythm. RN noted pallor on the client's face. At 1:42PM the client stated he was "a little bit dizzy" denied any other s/s of an allergic reaction. The client was offered water and began drinking it. No medications administered. Client denied any chronic conditions or medications and no known allergies. He began eating some goldfish at 1:45 PM. RN provided education to client and his parents regarding s/s of anaphylaxis, when to seek EMS, to follow up with PCP regarding syncope event, and V-safe. The client and his parents voiced understanding of this. Vitals obtained by EMT at 1:50 were BP 122/90, HR 72, RR 20. Repeat vitals obtained at 2:00PM were BP 122/86, HR 64, and RR 16. The client departed the vaccination site at 2:05 with his parents unassisted with a steady gait. The client's parents drove him home.

My appointment was on time, 4pm on 4/3 at the Pharmacy.  The young girl that gave me the shot told me she was certified, and she gave me the shot in the presence of her manager.  I have given  myself shots for years with diabetes, plus many flu shots, and have never felt pain like that.  I expressed this to her, how painful it was, and she just said "I know, I know..." as if it was normal for the shot to be so painful. I knew instantly something was wrong.  They were more worried, it seemed, about a potential adverse reaction such as an allergy shock, since I'm allergic to a few things, but I did not experience that.  I waited 15 minutes, my arm hurting the whole time, and they suggested I go buy Tylenol for the pain, which I did.  My left arm has hurt since then. I got a horrible bruise from this shot (will send picture) that took weeks to heal.  Since then I've continued to feel pain and don't have full mobility of my left arm. I can type, but not lifting anything heavy and have to go easy with anything on the left side.  I thought at first it might be what people were calling "covid arm" but I discovered that was more about soreness, not pain.  I tried ibuprofin, but after three weeks I'd had enough and made a doctors appointment.  Since I was also noticing my left shoulder was very tense and tight, and I was starting to get neck stiffness in same area, I started googling before my appointment.  When I entered my symptoms, SIRVA kept popping up, so I wondered if that was what I now had because of the improper vaccine administration.  I asked my doctor for an MRI order to find out, but she said we needed to do an Xray first (which only showed mild issues related to osteo).  She offered a prescription of taking Advil 400 mg three times and day and to use a muscle relaxer when I needed it, such as at night (Cyclobenzaprine).  She said to try that for a week, and if it wasn't better, that another Dr could order MRI.  Since then I've also added a pain spot under my left shoulder blade. Insurance called and said the order was "under review" so that's where things stand now. If they don't approve, I guess I will go next to an orthopedist for guidance?  This has cost me health, due to lack of sleep also - I wake up with pain in the middle of the night, even when I take the meds. Praying for a diagnosis, and solution, soon.

I received the vaccine shot at approximately 2:30pm in the afternoon on 9/13/21. Around 8pm that same evening, I started having very intense chills and my whole body felt freezing. I then started to experience whole body shaking similar to what women experience post-childbirth. This lasted for about 30-60 minutes. I also developed an intense headache and I became extremely tired. I took 800mg of ibuprofen and 1000mg extra strength Tylenol and went to bed at 9pm. My headache became worse overnight and pretty much lasted all night. My body hurt all over and the aches were so intense that I tossed and turned all night because I could not get comfortable. I have a 6 month old so when she woke up at 2am I went to tend to her. I came back to bed and my head hurt so badly that I couldn't really fall back asleep. I took 1/4 tablet of a doxylamine succinate tablet (unisom) and tried to go back to bed. At 5:40am my daughter awoke again so I got up to go tend to her. When I got into her room (which is down the hall) I picked her up and as I went to sit down in the rocking chair my vision started going out. By that I mean it got blurry, I started seeing spots, I felt very flushed/hot/sweaty/nauseous. Eventually I couldn't see at all. I almost threw up but didn't. I was able to stand up and put my daughter back in her crib and then I must have passed out or fallen on the floor because my husband heard a "thud" from down the hall. He came down to her room and asked if everything was OK. I could hear him but still could not see anything. I told him that I didn't feel well at all. He had to pick me up and carry me down the hall back to our bedroom because I could barely walk. At this point my vision was still gone - I literally could not see anything. I got very hot and flushed. My husband checked my temperature but I was not feverish. Clammy skin. I must have had a vagal response of some sort even though I had drank lots of water the previous day. In total my vision was probably black for at least 5 minutes, if not 10 minutes. My vision finally started to come back and my body temperature returned to normal. I continued to lay on the floor and I then had the worst headache of my life. It felt like my head was in a vice - it throbbed and was 11/10 on the pain scale. My husband helped me back to bed and I laid there for another hour until I felt well enough to get up and go downstairs. I took 800mg ibuprofen and 1000mg of Tylenol around 7:30am for my headache and drank a tall glass of water. My body continued to ache the rest of the day.

symptom_text: Starting 01/10/2022, I developed a rash across my chest and upper back, and a sore throat. On 01/11/2022, I went to work and I felt a little off but not enough to be off. I left in the middle of the day not feeling well. I had a fever spiking at around 102, a headache and body aches, joint pain and sore throat which worsened. The cough started either that night or the next day (01/12/2022). For about 3-4 days I would experience the same symptoms but nonstop. I tested positive on 01/12/2022. My temp started to subside around 01/15/2022 and it would remain at about 99F-100F for about a week. I still felt fatigued, body aches, cough, sore throat and runny nose until about 01/28 or 01/29. Then, I returned to work on 01/31/2022. It wasn't until then I noticed the "brain fog" which lasted for about a month. The last week of January my taste seemed to change and things started tasting funny/metallic. To this day, my taste has not returned and I have lost about 40 lbs due to being unable to tolerate most foods: dairy tastes sour/spolied, meat tastes rancid/bad, everything else has a chemical/dirt taste (breads and vegetables) and I am unable to tolerate sweets (make me nauseous). Also, around the 2nd week of being sick I developed extreme coldness in my hands and feet which would require extremely hot temperatures to rewarm them. To this day, I still get episodes of tingling coldness in my hands and feet but more intermittent (about 1x weekly now). During this episode, someone gave me a pulse ox to monitor my oxygen levels and the lowest they ever went were about 90% and, at that time, I was having shortness of breath and feeling very fatigued.

symptom_text: Patient was extremely tense on arrival at clinic and curt during all interactions with us. We proceeded with vaccination and immediately upon withdrawal of the vaccine syringe needle from the patient's left deltoid the patient stood up and began yelling and cursing while slamming the wall with his fist(s?) and forearm(s?), with elbow raised at sternal or neck-height and fist above, while exclaiming that his arm hurt badly and we had "hit something" in his arm.  Due to scene safety concerns we asked him to follow us out of the clinic, and we walked out of the clinic with him. Once outside of the clinic he seemed to feel unwell and stood leaning forward, we tried to help him sit down, and he later sat with his back leaned against the wall outside. Patient was alert, PWD, nothing seemed obviously medically-abnormal aside from his reported arm pain and level of stress and agitation, vitals not attempted due to scene safety concerns. We offered him a water, which he refused.  When asked for more information while again seated, the patient elaborated that upon vaccination he'd felt an instant shooting pain in his left arm, which within less than one second had radiated up the left posterior side of his neck, and he further stated that he had a tingling sensation in his left hand only (we think he slammed that hand into the wall, with a closed fist and ulna and ulnar styloid process experiencing most of the force from impacting the wall). We were unable to inspect the hands of the patient for injury signs due to safety concerns. The patient stated he had violent impulses he was suppressing. When asked if he had previously experienced pain like this from an injection, he stated he had never experienced something like this before. We inspected his arm and it appeared that the vaccination was done in the proper area of his left deltoid, and no band-aid had been applied due scene safety concerns after the vaccine had been injected. We offered him an ice-pack for the area, which he refused.  The patient stood up, and the patient stated and/or gestured that it hurt to raise his left arm. We instructed him to try moving it and raising it more as that generally helps, and after a few attempts he seemed to be able to raise it more. He remained alert and dexterous enough to use his smartphone to take a photo of his vaccine card. He stated his arm still hurt.  The patient then chose to leave. He left our view, and we think we heard him striking something as he departed, possibly the wall, but we could not see which part of his body, if any, struck something, nor which sort of object may have been impacted, nor what sort of injury pattern could have resulted from those actions. He then apparently walked out of the area of the clinic.

At this point I still have a pretty bad headache and painful body aches, specifically in my lower back and legs; fall back asleep * 8am-9am: Wake up and take more Advil. My whole body hurts. Toss and turn for a bit more. Small fever?99 degree temperature. Make coffee but have absolutely no appetite. * 9am-10am: So sweaty, fever is fully breaking * 11am: No more fever, slight headache, and body aches seem to be subsiding * 11:45am: Almost exactly 24 hours later and feeling good, comparatively speaking. Finally eat a bagel * 5:30pm: After lunch, I took a nap. My body aches have completely subsided, no fever. I still have a small headache and my ears still ache. But overall, I feel pretty normal!
